clue.text: Modern kind of port toured by crewman's "other half"

indicators.note: a place toured by someone has that person going all round it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a hand is a member of a ship's crew
a USB port is the modern computer socket

explanation.surface: A sailor's partner is pictured visiting a newly built harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts towards harbours or wine, but here it is the computer socket, sitting inside the crewman.
explanation.definitionFit: Other half is the jokey idiom for a spouse, and a married man is his wife's other half.

clue.text: Regular dress for sister, not even used

indicators.note: dropping the even-numbered letters keeps only the first, third and so on

blocks.note: a nun's robe is her habit
the odd-placed letters of the word

explanation.surface: A nun's everyday outfit, it seems, has gone to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' is a nun, whose robe is a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is a frequent visitor to a place, the noun sense of a regular customer.

clue.text: Airmen read slanderous spread featuring queen

indicators.note: spread suggests the words are scattered and laid out afresh
featuring means including something within, so a letter is set inside the rest

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess

explanation.surface: Pilots peruse a scurrilous tabloid story about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a newspaper feature, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Squadron leaders are officers in an air force, so they are airmen.

clue.text: Source of fire poorly restricted in vessel?

indicators.note: something restricted in a space is held inside it

blocks.note: an artery is a blood vessel
poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: A fire on a ship that was badly contained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is the blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the big guns of an army, which open fire on the enemy.

clue.text: Reverberations from marriages we'd abandoned

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: marriage ceremonies
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Echoes of the wedding bells after a couple called it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding is the ringing sound of a bell, the noise left reverberating after a strike.

clue.text: Prod guards with single part of body

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it protectively

blocks.note: a jab is a quick poke
W is the abbreviation for with
single means one

explanation.surface: A sharp poke defends a lone piece of anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: W for with is a standard abbreviation, as in bridge notation.
explanation.definitionFit: The jawbone, or mandible, is a bone of the human skeleton.

clue.text: Trendy traveller's black dog

blocks.note: jet black is a deep black
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A fashionable tourist owns a dark-coated hound.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is a wealthy, fashionable person who flies around the world for pleasure.

clue.text: Twisted insult

blocks.note: first meaning: coiled, past tense of wind (rhyming with find)
second meaning: to hurt someone's feelings (rhyming with spooned)

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound is the past of wind, as a coiled spring, and also a verb meaning to injure or offend.

clue.text: Editor with handwoven pants is finished for good!

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are in a poor state and must be reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor's handmade trousers are worn out for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but in British slang it means rubbish, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and done with is an idiom for something completely ended and put behind one.

clue.text: Final portion of text remembered

indicators.note: a portion is a part taken from a larger whole, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the last part of a passage they learned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' looks like it belongs with 'portion', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme can mean furthest or last, as in the extreme end of a line.

clue.text: Traditional weapon forthright men trust in, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up out of order

blocks.note: blunt means plain-spoken
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Outspoken men put their faith in an old-fashioned arm, to their cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt instrument is the classic murder weapon of detective fiction, a heavy club-like object.

clue.text: Dog's head and tail wagging, going up and down

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
wagging means moving to and fro, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A happy dog bobbing its head and wagging its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes a dog, but only its first letter is used, joined to the word tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes water that rises and falls with the tides.

clue.text: Bird that female navigator found on lake

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing found on another is placed after it

blocks.note: she is the female pronoun
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan sea captain who sailed round the world

explanation.surface: A woman sailor turns up on a lake, perhaps spotting birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The navigator is Francis Drake, England's famous circumnavigator.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck's male is called a sheldrake, a large colourful duck.

clue.text: Breakaway union should follow it

blocks.note: surface reading: a splinter trade union or political secession
setter's reading: a runaway couple, after which a wedding is expected

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a labour or political body, but it is a marriage; the clue describes running away to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running off secretly to marry, so the marriage follows the escape.

clue.text: With high principles they arranged to host one visit

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order
to host is to take a guest inside, so other letters go within

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: Principled people arranged to put up a guest for a stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethically means in a morally upright way, describing conduct guided by high principles.

clue.text: Grass-like plant ultimately overruns border

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A weed eventually spreads over the edge of a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grassy-looking marsh plant with solid triangular stems.

clue.text: Possibly Federer's turn to provide cake

indicators.note: possibly marks the tennis player as one example of a wider class

blocks.note: Roger Federer, the tennis champion, is from Switzerland
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: It is the tennis star's turn to bring the cake to the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a sponge cake spread with jam and rolled into a spiral.

clue.text: Investor facing unknown menace

blocks.note: a bull is a stock market investor expecting prices to rise
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A financier confronts a threat he cannot identify.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully works as a verb, to intimidate or threaten someone weaker.

clue.text: Best place in the house for kippers?

definitions.text: Best place in the house for kippers?

blocks.note: surface reading: smoked herrings, suggesting a kitchen or larder
setter's reading: kippers are people having a kip, a British word for a nap, so the room where they sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for sleep, so kippers here are sleepers rather than fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The room in a home set aside for sleeping is where people take their kip.

clue.text: Comic partner told of gangster's resilience

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so it is the sound of the name that counts

blocks.note: Oliver Hardy, partner of Stan Laurel in the comedy double act
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.surface: A comedian's sidekick talks about a mobster's toughness.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were a classic film comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness and robust toughness, an old word for resilience.

clue.text: Non-professional caught in the act and arrested

indicators.note: something caught in something else is trapped inside it

blocks.note: a deed is an act
lay means amateur, not of a profession

explanation.surface: An amateur criminal is caught red-handed and taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrested' suggests police, but it means held up, as in arrested development.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest progress is to halt or hold it back, so arrested can mean held up.

clue.text: Handicaps attract defensive players

blocks.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it
backs are defenders in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A team with weaknesses tempts opposing defenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawbacks are disadvantages, things that hinder like a handicap.

clue.text: Short jacket's something brigade should get rid of

definitions.text: something brigade should get rid of

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: a blazer is a smart jacket

explanation.surface: A cropped jacket the uniformed brigade would like to throw out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brigade' is the fire brigade, whose job is to put out a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A blaze is a large fire, the thing a fire brigade is called to extinguish.

clue.text: Jack may be on this workforce

blocks.note: first meaning: a pole, as a flag such as the Union Jack flies on one
second meaning: the employees of an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as a worker's name, but it is a flag, the Union Jack being Britain's national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a pole for flying a flag, and also the body of people employed somewhere.

clue.text: Period Harry Potter's familiar with?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stretch of time
second meaning: what a young wizard knows, a magic incantation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' hints at a witch's animal companion, but here it just means acquainted.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of time and also a magic charm of the kind wizards cast.

clue.text: Protection for Labour — most top parties hope to get it

definitions.text: top parties hope to get it

blocks.note: an overall is a protective garment worn for manual work
the majority is the greater part

explanation.surface: Politics: the Labour Party and its rivals chase a winning share of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the political party, but it is manual work.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall majority is more seats than all other parties combined, the goal of any leading party at an election.

clue.text: Grasp flower setter's holding

indicators.note: something holding another thing has it within its grip

blocks.note: the setter speaking of her own possession
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker clutching a bloom in her hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's is the crossword-maker's way of saying my.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is a thorough command of a subject, as in a good grasp of it.

clue.text: Stole placed in case outside church

indicators.note: one piece sits outside another, wrapping round it

blocks.note: filed means put away in a document file
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A vestment was put in a box outside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a priest's scarf, but it is the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To filch is to pilfer something small, so filched is a past-tense synonym for stole.
